APP_SUBTITLE.message: AI-powered UX testing that navigates your site and tells you what sucks.

SIGHTED_A11Y_HELP.message: Let sighted personas read element roles and ARIA names alongside the screenshot.

DESCRIPTION_PLACEHOLDER.message: e.g. Someone with limited time who wants to get things done quickly and gets frustrated by unnecessary steps.

PERSONA_FIRST_TIME_DESC.message: A first-time visitor with zero context about this product, its competitors, or its vocabulary. Forms snap judgments in the opening seconds — if the page doesn't explain what it is and why they'd care, they're gone. Gets overwhelmed by dense UI, unclear calls to action, or anything that feels like work before they've decided it's worth their time.

PERSONA_POWER_USER_DESC.message: A fast, confident user who lives in tools like this all day. Expects keyboard shortcuts, bulk actions, dense information, and zero hand-holding. Gets visibly annoyed by intrusive modals, condescending tooltips, laggy interactions, or any UI that treats them like a beginner.

PERSONA_ACCESSIBILITY_DESC.message: A user who relies on assistive tech — screen readers, keyboard-only navigation, high-contrast modes. Judges the site on whether every control is reachable by Tab, whether labels and alt text convey real meaning, whether focus order is logical, and whether dynamic updates are announced. Gets stuck and frustrated anywhere contrast is poor, labels are missing, or focus silently vanishes.

PERSONA_NON_TECHNICAL_DESC.message: Someone uncomfortable with jargon, nested settings, or anything that looks like 'admin.' Wants plain-language labels, obvious next steps, and friendly feedback when something works. Intimidated by error messages and unfamiliar terms like 'workspace' or 'API key,' and will give up rather than guess what a cryptic button does.

PERSONA_ROASTER_DESC.message: A brutally honest, sharp-tongued critic with a gift for spotting UX flaws and a zero-tolerance policy for lazy design. Notices every awkward label, weird alignment, patronizing copy, and baffling interaction, and calls them out with dry wit. Not cruel for its own sake — just allergic to the bare minimum. Treats this session like stand-up material, not a bug report.

TEST_HINT.message: Try things like "Sign up for an account" or "Find the pricing page"
